julgado.behavior: flusher.py:93 creates `shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` per flusher process using only that process's subset of shards (`self.process_to_shards_map[process_index]`, lines 61-66, 83-84), and line 169 calls `buffer.flush_segments(now=now)` on that sub-buffer. In buffer.py:382-384, `shard_factor = max(1, len(self.assigned_shards))` and `max_segments_per_shard = math.ceil(max_flush_segments / shard_factor)`, applied as the per-shard fetch limit (line 390) and the backpressure threshold (line 411). The option `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` (default 500) is documented as "Maximum number of segments to fetch and flush per cycle". Because each sub-buffer sees only its own shard subset, each computes its own per-shard budget and can flush up to ~max_flush_segments, so the aggregate per cycle across P processes is ~P×max_flush_segments.

consequences.consequence: The global 'spans.buffer.max-flush-segments' cap (500) is broken: the aggregate per-cycle flush cap becomes ~P×500 with P flusher processes.
Memory loaded from Redis per cycle is multiplied by the number of flusher processes.
any_shard_at_limit backpressure becomes ~P× harder to trigger (aggregate threshold rises to ~P×max_flush_segments).

julgado.remainingDefect: When multiple flusher processes are used, each process's SpansBuffer(shards) computes max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards)) from only its subset of shards, so each sub-buffer can fetch/flush up to the full max_flush_segments (default 500) per cycle. Trigger: running the flusher with more than one process (P>1), where each process holds total_shards/P shards. The result is that the documented per-cycle cap is exceeded by roughly a factor of P: aggregate segments pulled from Redis and held in memory per cycle scale with the process count, and the any_shard_at_limit backpressure threshold is likewise inflated, so it engages later than intended.
